The retrieved evidence supports part of Marcus's reasoning without settling the combined assertion.
limitations: The natural-systems paper is historical context, not outcome evidence for August 2026.

from_speaker: The kind of math OpenAI is dealing with here
radically different from many (perhaps most) real-world problems
infinite training data effectively for free
our_interpretation: The comparison concerns the mathematics in the August 1 release and real-world tasks as understood when the post appeared.
I read verification as establishing a proposed answer's correctness, rather than guaranteeing that a search will discover an answer.
I read infinite and effectively free as a practically unrestricted supply of correct, relevant examples at very low marginal cost.
Many means multiple substantial classes of real-world tasks. Perhaps most is a qualification, not a firm majority claim.
The post supplies no reporting period. I use August 1–2, covering the release being discussed and the post.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes both a substantial verification advantage for the mathematics represented in the release and a practically unrestricted, inexpensive supply of correct training examples, with documented limitations on both advantages across multiple substantial real-world task classes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that a central asserted advantage does not hold for the mathematics represented in the release, or that the claimed broad distinction from real-world tasks is false.
